label: t3-lumen-alt
topic: Track 3 alternatives and neighbours: lumen geometry (MDCK cyst lumen shape, Vasquez 2021)
summary: Keep MDCK (Vasquez 2021) as the primary system. Seven further candidates were screened beyond the four the scout already ranked (blastocyst, pancreatic organoids, zebrafish otic vesicle, bile canaliculus): zebrafish Kupffer's vesicle, ascidian notochord tube, intestinal organoids, a phase-field organoid model, Hydra spheroids, kidney-cell fluid pumps, and electrically inflated kidneyoids. None of the new ones is a better primary. Only the notochord (21.2 GB of images, MATLAB code with no licence field) and the kidney pump (source data in the article, plotting code on GitHub) have public material bearing on lumen mechanics, and neither pairs per-sample shape tables with a model sweep the way Vasquez does. Strongest competing explanation: pressure-dominated lumens (Laplace sphere, hydraulic inflation), refined by Mukenhirn 2024 into a pressure versus junctional-tension force balance in MDCK-II cysts. It is not independent of the chosen model: Vasquez's own model includes pressure and covers the pressure-dominated case, and Mukenhirn also reports excess apical area aiding lumen opening. The discriminating prediction is non-sphericity at low pressure, which a pure Laplace model cannot produce. I found no public per-cyst data for the Mukenhirn model, so it can be run only as a model arm on Vasquez data. Run alongside: the scout's pancreatic organoid tables (a higher-pressure regime where the rival should do better) as a regime check; do not add a dataset from this report as a gate. Registry note: law set 1.8.1 contains physiology-laplace (accepted) and no cell-geometry or lumen law; the seven cell-geometry candidates the earlier law-mapper cited are not in this tree.
lay_summary: Scientists want to know why the hollow centre of a tiny ball of kidney cells has the shape it has. One idea is that fluid pressure inflates it like a balloon, so it should be round. The chosen study found the shapes are often irregular, because the cells have a fixed amount of inner surface that they must fit around. I looked for other living systems that could test the same question, such as a fish embryo organ, the tube inside a sea squirt, and gut organoids. Each is either too large to download, has no public measurements, or is only a computer model, so I recommend keeping the kidney-cell balls as the main test. The balloon idea stays as the rival to beat, and a data set from pancreas organoids, where pressure matters more, is the best companion run.

findings.claim: Vasquez 2021 reports MDCK lumen shape reflects cell geometry tied to polarity, and its model includes both geometry and pressure.
findings.evidence_quote: We find that in this system, lumen shape reflects basic geometrical considerations tied to the establishment of apico-basal polarity. A physical model incorporating both cell geometry and intraluminal pressure can account for our observations

findings.claim: The pressure-dominated view is the competing explanation, supported by the mouse blastocyst.
findings.evidence_quote: Hydrostatic pressure has been proposed to drive lumen expansion, a view that is supported by experiments in the mouse blastocyst.

findings.claim: Mukenhirn 2024 (MDCK-II cysts) explains lumen morphologies from a pressure versus tension force balance and suggests excess apical area helps lumen opening, so the rival partly agrees with the chosen model.
findings.evidence_quote: enabled us to explain lumen morphologies from the pressure-tension force balance.

findings.claim: Mukenhirn 2024: ZO depletion collapses the lumen and folds apical membrane; claudin ion barrier is not required for inflation.
findings.evidence_quote: the depletion of the zonula occludens scaffold resulted in lumen collapse and folding of apical membranes

findings.claim: Kupffer vesicle: cell volume and shape changes are separable from lumen forces, so it argues against pressure alone controlling cell shape.
findings.evidence_quote: asymmetric changes in KV cell volume and shape occur normally when KV lumen growth fails due to leaky cell adhesions

findings.claim: The eLife record for the Kupffer vesicle paper lists no data files: additionalFiles holds only a transparent reporting form.
Ascidian notochord paper builds a conservation-law tube-expansion theory with asymmetric cortex tension and tight-junction gating, and predicts growth kinetics under different conditions.
findings.evidence_quote: a conservation-laws-based tube expansion theory was developed

findings.claim: Notochord images on Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15005334 total 21,226,936,940 bytes in 6 files under CC-BY-4.0, far above the 150 MB cap.
Notochord code is the public GitHub repo WenjieShi8514/Physics_tube, 11 files, MATLAB and Mathematica, no licence reported by the API.
Intestinal organoid paper: feedback between cellular tension and fluid pressure gives bulged versus budded crypt bistability.
findings.evidence_quote: bistability arising from feedback between cellular tensions and fluid pressure could be a general mechanism that coordinates multicellular shape changes in developing systems.

findings.claim: Intestinal organoid data statement: Source Data with the paper; code from an earlier MIT-licensed repo.
findings.evidence_quote: Data availability Source data are provided with this paper. Code availability Codes used in the current study are from previous work

findings.claim: Phase-field organoid model ships source code only, no measurements.
findings.evidence_quote: All source code for the model is available on GitLab at https://gitlab.com/Sakurako_T/hfsp .

findings.claim: Phase-field model gives phase diagrams in proliferation time and lumen pressure.
findings.evidence_quote: construct phase diagrams and show their dependencies on proliferation time and lumen pressure.

findings.claim: Hydra spheroid Zenodo record is 186,708,955 bytes, above the 150 MB cap, and holds expression data and scripts.
Hydra: osmotically driven inflation and deflation cycles stretch the tissue.
findings.evidence_quote: periodic osmotically driven inflation and deflation cycles generate mechanical stimuli in the form of tissue stretching

findings.claim: Kidney epithelial pumps: flux falls with hydraulic pressure until a stall pressure; ADPKD cells reverse flux direction.
findings.evidence_quote: The fluidic flux declines with increasing hydraulic pressure until a stall pressure, in a manner similar to mechanical fluid pumps.

findings.claim: Kidney pump data: source data with the paper, remainder on request.
findings.evidence_quote: available in the article and in the Supplementary Information and from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

findings.claim: Electro-inflation at about 5-10 V/cm inflates hollow kidneyoids and gut organoids, building hydrostatic pressure against cytoskeletal tension.
findings.evidence_quote: physiological-strength electrical stimulation of ∼ 5 - 10 V/cm powerfully inflates hollow tissues

findings.claim: Hydro-osmotic coarsening theory predicts lumen number N(t) proportional to t^(-2/5) under hydraulic coarsening; it concerns many-lumen cavity formation, not single-lumen shape.
findings.evidence_quote: dynamic scaling law N ( t ) ∝ t - 2 5 .

findings.claim: A 2026 review frames lumens as active and says models link molecular perturbations to lumen shape.
findings.evidence_quote: theoretical modeling and numerical simulations provide a quantitative framework for predicting phenotypes related to lumen shape

findings.claim: physiology-laplace bounds pressure by wall strength, thickness and radius and has no instance.
findings.evidence_quote: a wall that holds at most sigma_max limits the pressure to 2 sigma_max t / r (sphere) or sigma_max t / r (cylinder).

findings.claim: Discrepancy with the earlier law-mapper: it cited seven cell-geometry candidate laws in its 1.6.0 tree; I find none in the 1.8.1 repo.

key_claims.claim: Vasquez 2021 reports MDCK lumen shape reflects cell geometry tied to polarity, with a model that nests pressure; the pressure-dominated lumen is the competing view.
key_claims.evidence_quote: We find that in this system, lumen shape reflects basic geometrical considerations tied to the establishment of apico-basal polarity.

key_claims.claim: The strongest published rival is the pressure versus junctional-tension force balance of Mukenhirn 2024 in MDCK-II cysts, which also reports excess apical area aiding lumen opening.
key_claims.evidence_quote: explain lumen morphologies from the pressure-tension force balance

key_claims.claim: The best-documented new alternative, the notochord, ships 21.23 GB of images (6 Zenodo files) plus unlicensed MATLAB code, so it cannot be a bounded-cost companion.
Law set 1.8.1 has no cell-geometry or lumen law besides accepted physiology-laplace.

recommendations: Keep MDCK (Vasquez 2021) as the primary Track 3 system; none of the seven new candidates has per-sample shape tables plus a model sweep.

Implement the pressure-only Laplace sphere and a pressure-plus-junctional-tension variant as explicit rival model arms scored on the same Vasquez data; the pressure-tension arm needs per-cyst pressure, which Vasquez does not provide, so it must use a genotype-level pressure constant.
Run the scout pancreatic organoid tables alongside as a regime check (higher pressure, where the rival should do better); a model that wins in MDCK and loses there is a coherent result.

Do not add the notochord (21.2 GB), Hydra (186.7 MB, expression data) or Kupffer vesicle (no public data) to the gate. Optionally pull the kidney-pump Source Data (small) to put a pressure scale on the Laplace arm.
Ask the registry owner why the seven cell-geometry candidate laws are absent from 1.8.1: any lumen certificate would currently rest on physiology-laplace alone, which has no instance.
Try to obtain Mukenhirn 2024 per-cyst pressure and tension values (Dev Cell data statement not read); this is the single most valuable missing item.
